src/application/order-service.ts: advance() and cancel() hand state changes to order.advanceTo(state), order.cancel() and product.release(line.quantity).
src/application/order-service.ts: toDto() maps a domain Order to an application OrderDto, which is a normal application-layer job.

src/application/order-service.ts: the stock check before reserving (`if (product.stock < quantity) throw ...`) in place() is borderline domain logic. It is used to check several aggregates before any of them is changed.

parsedVerdict.reasoning: OrderService is an application-layer use-case service, and what it does fits that layer. It loads aggregates through repository ports defined in the domain, calls domain behaviour (product.reserve, product.release, order.advanceTo, order.cancel, new Order), persists the results through those ports, and maps entities to DTOs. The file has no transport, framework or persistence-technology code: no HTTP, no SQL, no storage details. Generating an ID through an injected function and checking for a duplicate order are normal orchestration tasks. One borderline point: in place(), the service merges quantities per product and checks stock (product.stock < quantity) before reserving anything. This could be seen as an invariant that belongs in the domain. However, the actual reservation is still done by Product.reserve. The up-front check across several aggregates reads as orchestration: it validates everything before changing anything. It does not replace a domain rule, so I don't count it as a clear violation.
